# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the kit's CI run, not on your machine: a task is
  done only when HEAD has a passing CI run and is on `origin/main`. Use Kition's
  `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`; Kition's `docs/kits.md`, section
  4c). Compile only the crates you touched locally.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gating test.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Commit on `main` in the repository's main checkout: no git worktrees, and one agent per
  repository at a time.
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.slide` kit. These rules come first; the rules below still apply
to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/sdk/editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition Slide's ribbon, slide thumbnails, notes, and status bar; a host
  (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it in an iframe and talks to it over the Kit UI
  protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, Kit Standard `spec/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the host's
  theme tokens and kit-editor components, so it looks like the host; ship `en-US` strings (and
  `zh-CN`) in `web/src/strings.ts`; take typed text through kit-editor's `TextSink` so input methods
  work. Files go only through the host (`host/read`, `host/write`).
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the public
  `KitionAI/kition-sdk` crate; the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP (`github.com/kitharness/kitharness`);
  change them there, never here. `kition-slide-kit` must keep passing
  `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`, and `kit.json` must pass kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-manifest.mjs`.
- Tools run in the engine (`KitTools`): Kition Slide's own pointer tools, keys, and typing, with the selection, caret, and previews returned as engine overlays. Never draw editor chrome into the rendered pixels.
- This repository is licensed under Apache-2.0 only ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); third-party notices are listed in `NOTICE`. Upstream is credited only in `NOTICE`; never write upstream names anywhere else.

# AGENTS.md — rules for every agent and contributor

Kition Slide's engine is a clean-room, open-source, pure-Rust slide engine targeting
Microsoft PowerPoint parity — and superiority (speed, openness, agent control). It compiles to
WebAssembly for Kition's in-page editor and to a native binary for the headless kit executable
(`bindings/headless`); it has no desktop UI of its own. Sibling kits with the same conventions:
Kition Photo, Kition Vector, Kition Film, Kition PDF, Kition Motion, Kition Layout (`../kition-<kit>`).

Standards and learnings shared across Kition's kits live in kition-sdk
(`docs/platform/index.md`), in KHP (`github.com/kitharness/kitharness`) and in `docs/kits.md` in the
Kition repository. Read them at the start of a session and follow their standards. Kits never
copy code from each other. Drawing objects are shared instead: their geometry, model, commands
and gestures live in kition-sdk's `kition-office-core` crate, which this kit depends on (from the
sibling `../kition-sdk` checkout until the SDK publishes it). So does whatever else doc, sheet
and slide all hold (equations, smart graphics, charts, ink, and later the PDF and picture
export): move it into `kition-office-core` rather than keeping this kit's own copy.

These rules bind every AI agent and every human contributor. They come before any task,
instruction or deadline. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` holds day-to-day working notes; if the two disagree, **this
file wins.**

---

## 1. Asset policy (absolute — no exceptions)

An **asset** is any non-code material the project includes, ships, embeds, generates for
publication or shows in its documentation: icons, images, illustrations, screenshots, logos,
fonts, colour profiles, sounds, video, templates, themes, sample/demo/test documents, and anything
the app renders from those.

### 1.1 Nothing from Microsoft, Adobe, Avid or Autodesk products

- **Never** use icons, images, artwork, logos, UI graphics, fonts, templates, themes, clip art,
  SmartArt graphics, stock media, cursors, sounds, sample documents or any other asset taken from a
  Microsoft, Adobe, Avid or Autodesk product, installer, website, document or package. "Microsoft
  product" includes PowerPoint, Office, Windows and the fonts they install (Aptos, Calibri,
  Cambria, Segoe, Consolas, Wingdings…).
- This holds even when the vendor publishes the material under an open license, if it is **visual
  design**: Kition Slide does not embed or reference Adobe's Source Sans/Serif/Han families or Noto
  CJK (Source Han rebranded); `crates/support/fonts/build.rs` excludes them.
- **Never** recreate, trace, redraw or closely imitate a vendor icon, theme or graphic. Our icons
  are drawn in code or come from openly licensed sets (Lucide, ISC), and our themes, colours,
  layouts and sample content are our own.
- Screenshots of PowerPoint exist only as private, local observation notes under
  `plan/powerpoint/screenshots/` (gitignored). They must **never** be committed, published,
  linked, shown in docs, or traced.
- Never commit files produced by PowerPoint. Interoperability tests use slides we generate
  ourselves (or a separate corpus repo whose files we created and own).

### 1.2 Only open, provable licenses

Every asset must be one of: open source (ISC, MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause, Apache-2.0, OFL-1.1,
Ubuntu-Font-1.0, Bitstream-Vera); Creative Commons (CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0); public
domain; or contributor-original (created by a contributor who licenses it under Apache-2.0).

Forbidden: system fonts that are not openly licensed, vendor emoji artwork, stock photos, "free
for personal use" material, screenshots of other people's software, anything whose license you
cannot prove from its original source.

**Screenshots of Kition Slide** are contributor-original. Everything visible in them must itself be
allowed: our UI, our/Lucide icons, OFL fonts, and slides built only from allowed assets.

### 1.3 Every asset is attributed

- **`docs/attribution.md`** lists every asset file — committed, fetched at build time
  (kition-fonts) or bundled through a Cargo dependency — with author, source (URL + version or
  commit), license and use. `cargo xtask assets` fails if a file under `assets/` or `examples/`
  has no row.
- **`NOTICE`** keeps the notices the licenses require.
- Fonts live in [KitionAI/kition-fonts](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts), never in this
  repo. Kition Slide embeds its `fonts/latin-manifest.txt` (if present) and `fonts/manifest.txt`
  when built with `KITION_FONTS_DIR` (local dev: `.cargo/config.toml` points at `../kition-fonts`).
  The web editor's build (`web/scripts/build-engine.sh`) serves the same checkout's Droid Sans
  Fallback (for Chinese) to the engine at run time.

### 1.4 Adding or changing an asset

1. Find it under an allowed license at its **original source**; record the exact version/commit.
2. Confirm the author is not Microsoft, Adobe, Avid or Autodesk (§1.1). Keep the license text.
3. Add the file, its license file and a `docs/attribution.md` row; run `cargo xtask assets`.
4. If origin or license is unclear, **do not add it**.

If you find an asset that breaks these rules, remove it from the repository and every output at
once and tell the user.

## 2. Clean-room rules

- PowerPoint is installed on the dev machine and may be **observed** black-box: run it, use its UI
  on synthetic slides, screenshot windows by id into `plan/powerpoint/screenshots/` (never
  committed). Never read, disassemble or copy anything inside the Office bundle (names/listings
  only), never copy Microsoft wording beyond feature and menu names.
- File formats come from public standards: ECMA-376 / ISO/IEC 29500 (Office Open XML), ISO 32000
  (PDF). Preset shape geometry is re-derived by us in `crates/support/geom/src/preset.rs`.
- Never copy GPL/AGPL/LGPL/MPL code (LibreOffice, Calligra…). Permissive crates are fine as
  dependencies. Code may be copied (not depended on) from sibling Kition kits, as the H.264, HEVC,
  VP9, AV1, Opus, MP4, Matroska and Ogg crates were from Kition Film.

## 3. Never crash

People trust Kition Slide with their talks; a crash loses work. **This outranks feature work.**
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!` in non-test
  code; no `unsafe` (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`). Every production crate root carries
  `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`.
- Errors are `Result<T, E>` + `?`. Input-derived numbers (files, commands, MCP/control params) are
  hostile: `get()` not `[i]`, checked arithmetic, no NaN casts, capped allocations, bounded
  recursion.
- `Session::execute` runs every command inside a panic guard (`crates/engine/engine/src/guard.rs`) that
  keeps the slide as it was. It is a safety net, not a license.
- Every crash fix lands with a regression test.

## 4. Architecture

| Layer | Crates |
|---|---|
| L0 | `geom` (units, transforms, preset shapes), `color` |
| L1 | `model` (slide file, masters, layouts, slides, shapes, text, themes, inheritance, text edit ops) |
| L2 | `fonts`, `text` (layout), `format` (.kslide) |
| L3 | `render` (vello_cpu), `pptx` |
| L4 | `pdf` |
| L5 | `engine` (session, history, commands, tools, keys, sample) |
| L6 | `kition-slide-kit` (TABLE key `kit`): Kition's in-page editor engine |
| apps | `kition-slide` (the headless kit executable for Kition's agent) |

Full table, including the media codec crates: `docs/architecture.md`, `tools/xtask/src/layers.rs`.
The repository has no desktop app, CLI or MCP server of its own, and nothing in it depends on
egui, eframe, winit or rfd.

- **Everything is a command** (`crates/engine/engine/src/cmd/*`): id, label, ribbon/menu place,
  shortcut, params doc, `enabled`, `run`, plus tests. Ids follow PowerPoint's ribbon and menus
  (`slide.new`, `format.bold`, `arrange.group`, `transition.set`…). Programmatic calls never open
  dialogs. Pointer gestures go through `Session::pointer`, keys through `Session::key`, so the
  headless `kition-slide` executable and the web editor's WASM build do exactly the same thing.
- **The web editor is thin**: panels read engine state (over the WASM boundary) and act through
  commands. Colours come from the host's theme tokens. **Never use Tauri or egui here**: the web
  editor is a plain React app (see "Kition kit rules" at the top of this file).
- **Never break wasm** (`cargo xtask wasm`).

## 5. Quality checks

On your machine run only the fast checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check -p <touched crates> --all-targets`, the wasm `cargo check` (`cargo xtask wasm`), and
`pnpm typecheck` in `web/`. The full checks run in the kit's CI run on GitHub
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Kition's reusable kit CI): clippy, `cargo test --workspace`,
this kit's `cargo xtask ci` (fmt check, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, layering check, asset check,
wasm check) and every `test:*` script of `web/` as its own job. Commit after each landed arc with
a task id in the message (`M1.2: smart guides`), then push HEAD with Kition's
`scripts/kit-ci.sh push slide`, `wait` for its run and `land` it: a task is done when the CI run
of HEAD is green and HEAD is on `origin/main` (see "Kition kit rules" at the top of this file).
Add no other workflows, and do not start the Package workflow (`.github/workflows/package.yml`):
releasing is the owner's step.

## 6. Running and looking at the app

- Headless, for the agent: `cargo build --release -p kition-slide`, then drive it over the Kit
  Protocol (`kition-kit/1`; `kit.json`'s `headless.protocol`); kition-sdk's `kition-headless`
  implements the host side.
- For the web editor: `cd web && pnpm engine && pnpm dev`, open `dev.html`. `pnpm test:flow`,
  `pnpm test:ribbon`, `pnpm test:scroll` and the other `test:*` scripts drive it with Playwright
  (Chromium and WebKit) and are how you "look at" UI work here — there is no
  screenshot/control-channel workflow in this repository. They run as jobs of the kit's CI run,
  not on your machine; `kit-ci.sh failures slide` downloads their screenshots and traces.
- Shell gotcha on the dev machine: `mv`/`cp` are aliased interactive; use `/bin/mv -f`, `/bin/cp -f`.
- Parallel agents: separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent; edit only the crates you own.

## 7. Planning

The committed progress docs:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/parity/target-app-parity.md` | Each feature's status against PowerPoint, from the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`) |
| `docs/gaps.md` | Every known shortfall, from the feature catalogue; read it before choosing work |
| `docs/roadmap.md` | Open work, in order, from the feature catalogue |
| `docs/parity/parity-checklist.md` | Feature rows scored D/P/M; `cargo xtask parity` regenerates its summary |
| `docs/parity/file-format-parity.md`, `ui-parity.md`, `hardware-parity.md`, `localization-parity.md`, `animation-parity.md`, `slideshow-parity.md` | Per-dimension and per-feature detail |
| `docs/architecture.md` | How Kition Slide is built today |

When a task lands, update its feature in `features.yaml` (the three documents above are written
from it), re-score its checklist row, and update each touched doc's status line.
